title: When private 5G networks in manufacturing can complement Wi-Fi
summary: Explore how private 5G networks in manufacturing can complement existing Wi-Fi, with results informed by Belden and Betacom’s industrial connectivity testing.
body_markdown:
As more automated equipment moves across your plant, wireless performance can have a direct effect on production. Maintaining a connection now means supporting equipment along its entire route, including handoffs between access points. When those handoffs interrupt communication, equipment may have to pause before it can continue. Even where coverage is available, **inconsistent response times can make it harder to support applications that depend on prompt data exchange.**


If your plant’s existing Wi-Fi network can’t consistently meet these requirements, replacing it isn’t necessarily the answer. Instead, you need a way to strengthen connectivity for demanding applications without disrupting connections that already work.


Deploying private 5G networks in manufacturing could provide that additional connectivity alongside your existing plant Wi-Fi, giving you another way to **support automation without replacing the network you already have** .


## What private 5G networks bring to plant connectivity


As plants add more automation, private 5G is drawing interest as a way to support mobile equipment and timely data exchange alongside existing networks.


Private 5G networks in manufacturing rely on cellular technology but are dedicated to your organization, not shared with public mobile subscribers. They provide ultra-reliable connectivity and low latency for equipment that moves across a facility and depends on timely data transfer: predictive maintenance, IoT devices,[automated guided vehicles (AGVs)](https://www.belden.com/blog/6-tips-for-reliable-agv-wireless-networks-in-auto-manufacturing) , etc. Coverage and network policies can be configured around specific facility, devices and application requirements.


In manufacturing environments, equipment also needs a way to communicate over a private 5G network. It doesn’t need its own 5G connection to use the private network—it can **connect to an industrial router that sends and receives data over 5G** .
